question.prompt: If \(x=1+2^p\) and \(y=1+2^{-p},\) then \(y\) in terms of \(x\) is:

solutions.explanation:
The opposite exponents make \(2^p\) and \(2^{-p}\) reciprocals. Since \(x=1+2^p\), we have
\[
2^p=x-1,
\qquad 2^{-p}=\frac1{x-1}.
\]
For real \(p\), \(2^p>0\), so \(x>1\) and the denominator is nonzero. Substituting into the formula for \(y\) gives
\[
y=1+\frac1{x-1}
=\frac{x-1+1}{x-1}
=\frac{x}{x-1}.
\]
Thus \(\boxed{y=x/(x-1)}\), choice C.
solutions.title: Use the reciprocal relationship
